front: Why is abstinence the most effective method?
back: With no intercourse, sperm never enter the vagina and no body fluids are exchanged, so it prevents pregnancy and STIs.

front: Why are withdrawal and the rhythm method unreliable?
back: Sperm can be released before ejaculation, ovulation varies and sperm can survive for several days.
A thin sheath traps semen, so sperm cannot enter the uterus; it also reduces the spread of STIs, including HIV.
A dome over the cervix stops sperm entering the uterus; spermicide kills any sperm that get past it.
Placed in the uterus, its copper kills sperm and prevents an embryo implanting.

front: How do the pill, injection and implant work?
back: Their hormones stop ovulation and thicken the mucus at the cervix.
The sperm ducts are cut and tied, so semen contains no sperm; it is permanent.
The oviducts are cut and tied, so eggs and sperm cannot meet; it is permanent.
Using condoms with another method, to protect against both pregnancy and STIs.
